DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21 (independent auditor, authored none of 32ff59085b). Section 3.1: "Any other Route Types MUST be silently ignored upon a receipt if a BGP speaker supports only 3gpp-5G architecture type." The earlier weak finding (retainMUP summed Discarded and WithdrawnCount, so a recognizer answering Withdraw for unknown route types still passed) is answered: TestMUPOtherRouteTypesSilentlyIgnoredAtIngress now reads retainMUPCounts and asserts discarded == 4 and withdrawn == 0 separately, with the ISD between them kept byte for byte, under both MUP families. keyMUP keys an unknown route type on its whole NLRI, so a Withdraw answer would land in WithdrawnCount and go red; a Keep answer fails the kept equality. The negative TestMUPDefinedRouteTypesSurviveIngress (types 1 to 4, kept whole, nothing dropped) changed only by the T1ST body gaining its mandatory zero Source Address Length octet. TestRFCMUPUnknownRouteTypeIsNotRejected adds that ParseMUP skips an unknown route by its Length. RecognizeNLRI revert records re-observed red today on both polarities. The optional "MAY log" is not tested and not owed.

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.1.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21 (independent auditor, authored none of 32ff59085b). Section 3.1.1 ISD Prefix Length bound (32 under IPv4, 128 under IPv6) with treat-as-withdraw. The changed unit is the negative TestMUPWellFormedRouteKeptAtIngress: its two T1ST cases gained the zero Source Address Length octet and are now complete routes under the corrected parser; every other case, and every assertion (section kept whole, Withdrawn and Unkeyable empty, Discarded zero), is unchanged. The positive ISD cases (IPv4 33 withdrawn exactly; IPv6 129 discarded as unkeyable) and the negative ISD 32/128 cases are byte-identical. Both revert records were re-taken today with ./le rfc discriminate-record over HEAD and observed red naming the unit.

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.1.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21 (independent auditor, authored none of 32ff59085b). Section 3.1.1: "A BGP speaker MUST skip such NLRIs and continue processing of rest of the Update message." Positive keeps exactly L then L2 around every malformed shape. The changed unit is the negative TestMUPWellFormedRouteKeptAtIngress: its two T1ST cases gained the zero Source Address Length octet and are now complete routes under the corrected parser; every other case, and every assertion (section kept whole, Withdrawn and Unkeyable empty, Discarded zero), is unchanged. 32ff59085b made the T1ST Source Address Length octet mandatory, matching Section 3.1.3.1 ("The Source Address Length has a fixed length of 1 octet." and the TLV remainder counted from "the offset of the end of the Source Address"); parseBodyT1ST now returns ErrMUPTruncated when nothing follows the endpoint. Both revert records were re-taken today with ./le rfc discriminate-record over HEAD and observed red naming the unit.

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.1.3-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21 (independent auditor, authored none of 32ff59085b). Section 3.1.3: "If the AFI is IPv4, then the maximum value of the Prefix Length field is 32. If the AFI is IPv6, then the maximum value of the Prefix Length field is 128." 32ff59085b made the T1ST Source Address Length octet mandatory, matching Section 3.1.3.1 ("The Source Address Length has a fixed length of 1 octet." and the TLV remainder counted from "the offset of the end of the Source Address"); parseBodyT1ST now returns ErrMUPTruncated when nothing follows the endpoint. Positive T1ST IPv4 prefix length 33 now closes with endpoint4NoSource, so the prefix bound is the only fault and the route is withdrawn exactly; negative prefix 32 kept, now with its mandatory zero source length. The IPv6 128 clause has no T1ST case in the tagged units: parseBodyT1ST calls the shared AFI-indexed m.parsePrefixField, whose IPv6 bound the ISD 128/129 cases pin; a T1ST-only regression of that clause would stay green here, as the 2026-10-14 judgement already noted. Both revert records were re-taken today with ./le rfc discriminate-record over HEAD and observed red naming the unit.

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.1.3.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21 (independent auditor, authored none of 32ff59085b). Section 3.1.3.1: "The TEID value of 0 is considered as an invalid and a malformed TEID.  A BGP speaker MUST handle such a malformed NLRI as a \"Treat-as-withdraw\" [RFC7606]." 32ff59085b made the T1ST Source Address Length octet mandatory, matching Section 3.1.3.1 ("The Source Address Length has a fixed length of 1 octet." and the TLV remainder counted from "the offset of the end of the Source Address"); parseBodyT1ST now returns ErrMUPTruncated when nothing follows the endpoint. The positive T1ST TEID 0 case now ends in endpoint4NoSource, so with the TEID check removed the route would be complete and kept: TEID 0 stays the only fault (withdrawn exactly, siblings kept). Negative TEID 1 kept. Both revert records were re-taken today with ./le rfc discriminate-record over HEAD and observed red naming the unit.

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.1.3.1-10.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21 after 27b0796cea (independent auditor, authored none of it). Section 3.1.3.1: "any TLV parsing error MUST result in Treat-as-withdraw". The reactor unit's overrun case (TLV 0xF0 declaring Length 5 over one octet) is now preceded by K0 of the same RD and prefix, and asserts K leaves MP_REACH, siblings including L2's unknown TLV kept byte for byte, and the route withdrawn in MP_UNREACH by K0's bytes, which the recognizer keeps. With Section 3.1.5's Type/Length/Value framing, an overrun and the one-octet header (3.1.3.1-7) are the parse errors that exist. TestMUPT1STTLVFraming (negative: overrun gives ErrMUPTLV; positive: well-framed TLV accepted) unchanged. Scoped go test green; ValidateNLRI record re-taken in 27b0796cea. Re-judged again 2026-10-21 after the review round 1 fix: the unit changed by one identifier only (assert.Nil on validation.typedWithdrawBodies, the renamed [][]byte), inputs and every other assertion unchanged. Producer re-read: typedNLRIWalk.withdrawal still answers a recognizer Withdraw with the held generation (now kept in typedNLRIHeldRoutes, session-private for a Session with no Peer), and typedNLRIPlaceWithdrawals appends it as MP_UNREACH_NLRI to the same UPDATE when it fits the message limit, else to separate withdraw-only bodies; the test pins the in-message path and still fails on a kept, dropped or malformed-bytes withdrawal. Negative subtest: well-formed L+L2 returned unchanged. TestMUPT1STMandatoryFieldsWithinLength unchanged since the 32ff59085b judgement. DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.3.6-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent auditor) after the receive recognizer changed. recognizerFor (mup/rfc7606.go) now runs RecognizeNLRI then ValidateNLRI, which checks the NLRI body alone: Retain hands it one NLRI and no path attributes, and no code in internal/component/bgp reads a Prefix-SID SRv6 locator or compares it with a DSD MP_REACH next hop, so a DSD route whose next hop and locator differ is still stored rather than treated as withdrawn. The {gap} annotation's phrase "reads the architecture and route type alone" is now out of date (the body is also validated), but its conclusion holds.

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.3.6-5.note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent auditor, after 691bd048e9). draft-ietf-bess-mup-safi Section 3.3.6: "When a BGP speaker receives a MP_REACH_NLRI attribute update message with a Direct Segment Discovery route without a prefix SID attribute, than it MUST be treated as if it contained a malformed prefix SID attribute and the "Treat-as-withdraw procedure of [RFC7606] is applied.  A BGP speaker MUST skip such NLRIs and continue processing of rest of the Update message." The earlier unimplemented verdict is superseded: mup/rfc7606.go::CheckDSDPrefixSID is registered by mup/register.go for both ipv4/mup and ipv6/mup through nlritype.RegisterUpdateCheck, and the receive path (Session.applyRFC7606 -> applyTypedNLRIDiscard -> typedNLRIEdit -> nlritype.RetainUpdate) moves an announced DSD route with no Prefix-SID out of MP_REACH_NLRI into MP_UNREACH_NLRI per NLRI, keeping its siblings and the session; typedNLRIUpdateAttrs counts a Prefix-SID that RFC 7606 attribute-discard removes (the RFC 8669 Section 4 EBGP rule) as absent. Tests drive whole hex UPDATE bodies through Session.enforceRFC7606 and assert exact bytes: TestMUPDSDWithoutPrefixSIDWithdrawnOnReceive (kept MP_REACH NLRI equals the ISD sibling, MP_UNREACH NLRI equals the DSD route, no error, for both an absent and an EBGP-discarded Prefix-SID) and TestMUPDSDWithPrefixSIDKeptOnReceive (DSD with a Prefix-SID, and ISD plus Type 2 ST without one, return RFC7606ActionNone and the UPDATE byte for byte). The recorded discrimination breaks are panics, which prove reach only, so five overlay mutants were run (go test -overlay, tags ze_core ze_bgp): Keep instead of Withdraw when the Prefix-SID is absent (positive red, both cases); withdraw a DSD even with a Prefix-SID (negative DSD case red); drop the route-type test so every type is withdrawn (positive and negative ISD/T2ST case red); Discard instead of Withdraw (positive red, "withdrawn, not dropped"); ignore attribute-discard entries in typedNLRIUpdateAttrs (positive EBGP-discard case red). All five killed. Residual: only AFI 1 is exercised; the AFI 2 family is covered by the same registration loop, not by a test. test/plugin/mup-dsd-without-prefix-sid-withdraw.ci exists but is untagged and was not run here.
